description: [roadmap S3.24] At the SECOND vertex of an antialiased line of width 3 or more (never at the first), Windows' generic GL leaves out, in some columns, the outermost pixel next to the end cap although it lies inside S3.8's support (t - L 0.31 .. 0.49): 20 of 1,016 visible past-cap pixels of the white probe set (log/roadmap/S3/24_capfit.py). In the canonical frame (major and minor increasing, origin at the second vertex) the dropped pixels sit at (u, v) = (-0.5, +1.5), (-0.5, +2.5), (-2.5, +3.5), (+1.5, -1.5), (+2.5, -4.5) ...; at (-0.5, +1.5) they are dropped for slopes 0.615 .. 0.65 (widths 3, 5, 10 alike) and drawn at 0.605 and below and at 0.667 .. 0.72 (24_capcol.py). Neither a cap test at a shifted sample point (24_capscan.py, best of 81 shifts errs on 47 of 52) nor a count from the window start (24_probe.py rule ecNN) separates them. In the census it leaves cov_a_build brush_465 (3 px, one level).
needed: The generic implementation's end-cap span arithmetic (more probes per slope at the last columns, or its code).

description: [roadmap S3.24] The span rule's tie convention (a pixel centre exactly at +-N/2) is fitted, not read from the implementation: s = o * sign(dx) * sign(dy) for x-major lines and o * sign(dx) for y-major lines in [-N/2, N/2) (line rule 2). It decides every 45-degree tie of the probes in all four directions and makes 29 of the 31 census rows of log/roadmap/S3/22_causes.tsv group 1 exact, but on the game-like probe sets 5 pixels are wrong that S3.8's model had right (24_newbad.py b8s1: 4 in syn_white, 1 in syn_game): exact ties of y-major lines whose side varies between lines of one octant, and two pixels 0.0007 / 0.0009 beyond N/2 that the real GL draws. Vertex precision models (rounding of the setup to 4 .. 20 bits, unrounded double / float32) do not explain them (24_tieprec.py: chance level).
needed: The generic implementation's minor-axis DDA (start rounding, slope bits); a dedicated tie probe set per slope and octant (24_probe.py synth ties).

description: [roadmap S3.24] The census rows were judged with the port's own drawLine ends (the recorded GL streams keep no glBegin..glEnd vertices, U-1373) and through framegate's frames only: the dumped calls (SG_OVERLAY_DUMP) span every frame of a run, so a dumped call is not tied to the checkpoint frame it belongs to; the census-harvested tie labels (24_harvest.py) are therefore not used as evidence.
needed: A frame index in the dump (development switch) if the ties are revisited.

description: [roadmap S3.24] cov_a_keys k_dlg_R keeps 1 px one level on a hole line after the span rule (class MID: neither tie, cut nor cap); the line's value arithmetic (U-1371) is the only candidate left and is not separated from the terrain below the line under GlRaster.
